critical_code_review_comments: routes_payroll.py is now 957 lines — exceeds the 700-line guideline. Consider splitting into modules: employees_crud.py (identity + periods + terminate/rehire + history), pay_settings.py, super.py, tax.py (owner-only), bank.py (owner-only), leave_balances.py, pay_items.py, leave_types.py — all sharing a small helpers module for _require_owner/_clean/_iso_or_none.

EmployeeProfile.jsx is 935 lines — same issue on the frontend side. Extract each tab into its own component (OverviewTab.jsx, EmploymentTab.jsx, PaySettingsTab.jsx, TaxTab.jsx, DocumentsTab.jsx, HistoryTab.jsx, TerminateDialog.jsx, RehireDialog.jsx).

In routes_payroll.put_tax(): sending tfn='' is treated as 'no change' — this is documented but non-obvious. A follow-up endpoint POST /employees/{id}/tax/clear-tfn (or a boolean 'clear_tfn': true flag) would let owners explicitly wipe a previously-stored TFN without ambiguity.

Mobile duplicate detection uses trailing 8 digits via regex on the raw mobile string. If the stored mobile contains non-digits (e.g. '+61 4xx xxx xxx' vs '04xxxxxxxx'), a substring regex on '04xxxxxxxx' will not match. Consider storing a normalised digits-only field (mobile_norm) at write time and matching against that — improves recall of the duplicate check.

list_employees performs a second query (employee_pay_settings) then builds the 'current' map in Python. For large tenants this is O(pay_history_rows). Could be moved to an aggregation with $group+$first sorted by effective_from desc for O(1) per employee at the DB layer.

GET /employees/{id}/history does not require owner role — even though it echoes termination_reason/termination_note fields which may be sensitive (HR notes). Consider gating with _require_owner or a dedicated 'hr_manager' role check.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (all 10 tabs render, all documented data-testids present, terminate dialog + document upload + notes save all verified live)
